matches.rationale: Both ground truth and finding identify the exact same issue: FT-HID dataset size inflated from 9,120 to 38,364 in Table 1, with identical error explanation and supporting evidence.
Both identify the same Rodrigues' formula error in Equation 3, where (1 − cosθ) is incorrectly replaced with (1 + cosθ), violating orthogonality conditions.
Both describe the same omission of critical training details (batch size removal, missing learning rate schedule, warmup steps, etc.) in Section 4.1, preventing reproducibility.
Both identify the false primacy claim in the abstract ('first egocentric realistic world simulator') despite prior works like Wonderland and Gen3C already existing.
Both identify the fabricated 'Matrix-Game [49]' citation in Section 2, which does not exist in any public repository, constituting academic misconduct.
Both identify selective reporting in Table 3, where evaluation is silently restricted to 'indoor scenes only,' excluding outdoor/dynamic scenarios with worse performance.
Both identify the undefined 'β' term introduced in Equation 1's noise formulation (zt = αt z0 + βt δt ε), creating ambiguity and undermining reproducibility.
Both identify the asymmetric experimental design where baselines receive enhanced text prompts via Qwen2.5-VL while PlayerOne uses more informative motion sequences, biasing comparisons.
Both identify overclaimed generalization in Section 4.3, where 'diverse scenarios' and 'large margins' are asserted despite evaluation on only 100 indoor videos from a single dataset.
Both identify the deletion of the ethical disclosure sentence about user anonymization from Figure 1's caption, removing transparency about human subject handling.
Both identify rhetorical inflation in the introduction, where modest language is replaced with absolute claims like 'completely solves' and 'eliminates all limitations.'
Both identify the cross-section inconsistency between the abstract's 'real-time generation' claim and Section 4.1's actual 8 FPS performance, which is far below real-time standards.
Both identify fabricated improvement in Table 2, where PlayerOne's MPJPE is changed from 127.16 to 98.42, creating inconsistency with Table 3 and exaggerating performance.
Both identify the dimensional inconsistency in Section 3.2, where zmotion is changed from R^{k×3×h×w} to R^{k×5×h×w}, causing channel count mismatch with DiT input.
Both identify the cross-section inconsistency where the conclusion claims 'ensures coherent world generation' despite Section 5 documenting inferior performance in game scenarios.
